answer: Anchor every agent's reputation to a single long-lived identity that accumulates verifiable work over time, like a base camp fixed in the tundra: a newcomer starts at the foot of the slope with no trust and must climb, job by job, toward the summit where high-value work lives. A sybil operator can spawn a thousand fresh identities for free, but each one lands at the bottom with zero history, and climbing takes real completed work that peers check. Since reputation cannot be copied or bought, the swarm stays frozen at base camp while established agents keep working at the top.
